title: Haiti was made to pay France for its own freedom
body: In August 1791, enslaved people in the French colony of Saint-Domingue rose up. After more than a decade of war, they declared independence on 1 January 1804, creating Haiti: one of the only states in history born from a slave rebellion and ruled by the formerly enslaved. But France withheld recognition, and the price Haiti was later forced to pay shaped its economy for more than a century.

slides.heading: Earliest first
items: The debt is cut to 60 million francs
The related loans are finally paid off
slides.explanation: The uprising began in 1791, independence came on 1 January 1804, France’s demand in 1825, the cut to 60 million in 1838, and the loans were cleared in 1947.

slides.heading: 1825: terms at gunpoint
slides.text: French warships delivered King Charles X’s terms: recognition for 150 million francs, to compensate ex-colonists for lost property, including enslaved people.

slides.heading: Borrowing to pay
slides.text: Haiti had to take out a loan just to make the first payment. In 1838 France cut the remaining debt to 60 million francs, but the loans carried interest of their own.

slides.heading: Paid off in 1947
slides.text: A 2022 New York Times analysis found the related loans were cleared only in 1947, after Haiti paid about 112 million francs, roughly 560 million dollars today.

slides.heading: Haiti’s debt to France, in millions of francs
slides.note: About 112 million francs by the 2022 New York Times analysis, roughly 560 million dollars today.
slides.explanation: Cut to 60 million in 1838, but Haiti borrowed to pay and the loans carried interest: about 112 million francs in all by 1947, nearly twice the reduced sum.
